transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-12 09:28 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Sara (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Chris (Redwood SE), John Ellis, Priya Rao, Marcus Chen, Aisha Bello (Meadowbrook)
Recording quality: typical conference call, some packet loss ~1-2%

Auto-summary: quick capture — customer is evaluating open-model options for customer-facing summarization & claims triage; heavy emphasis on PII and data residency; wants support for Spanish and French; needs tool-calling to internal claims APIs.

[00:00] Sara (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining from Meadowbrook, really appreciate you carving out time. we're Redwood Inference, I'm Sara, the AE on the account, with Diego and Chris from our solutions engineering team. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] John (Meadowbrook): good morning. thanks for doing this. big agenda for us — picking a model path and understanding deployment options.
[00:15] Priya: yeah we want something that can do summarization and also multi-lingual customer responses, and we have strong constraints on PII and residency.
[00:24] Diego (SE): great, we'll cover open model trade-offs, context windows, multilingual baselines, and then deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC. sound good?
[00:30] Aisha: yes. also interested in tool-calling — we need the model to call our claims system and redact data before calling external APIs.

[02:05] Chris (SE): quick qual — what are your current volumes / QPS? and what's the latency SLO you need for production?
[02:12] Marcus: right now it's low QPS in the pilot, maybe 2-3 TPS at peak, but we expect spikes during claims season up to ~25 TPS, and 95th pct latency should be under 400ms ideally for customer chat flows.
[02:25] Diego: ok that's helpful — 25 TPS peak maps cleanly to dedicated reserved pools but for pilot hosted can work. cost/latency trade-offs we'll sketch out.

[04:10] John: by "redact" we mean PII should never leave our VPC for the private option; for hosted, we need to understand encryption at rest and in-transit, and KMS integration. is that supported?
[04:22] Sara: yes — hosted has encryption, but for KMS customer-managed keys and full audit logs we typically recommend Dedicated or Private. I'll send our security whitepaper.
[04:45] Marcus: do you have SOC2? and do you expose audit logs per request?
[04:50] Sara: we are SOC2 Type II, and yes we can provide request-level audit logs for enterprise tiers.

[06:05] Diego: shifting to models — are you leaning open-source models or managed models (e.g. OpenAI)? and what accuracy/ hallucination tolerance do you have for claims summarization?
[06:18] John: we prefer open models where possible to avoid vendor lock-in and to control costs. hallucination tolerance is low — we need conservative outputs or citations from internal documents.
[06:30] Diego: got it. for open models we usually compare a handful of Llama-like and Mistral variants and also some 2- and 4-bit quantized versions for cost. for long context we look at 8k, 32k, and sometimes 64k if you have long claim threads. what are your context needs?
[06:45] Priya: most tickets are under 3k tokens, but some claim threads include policy history, attachments and can go past 20k tokens. so 32k would be ideal for the long-run.
[06:58] Chris: okay so 32k support plus KV / prefix caching is likely important so you don't pay for repeating headers every request.

[08:15] John: multilingual — English primary, Spanish second, occasional French. we need decent Spanish quality out of the box, possibly fine-tune with 50k examples.
[08:26] Diego: that helps. some open models have stronger English than Spanish; we can run a small eval suite. we also support on-the-fly translation toolchains if needed.

[09:30] [audio glitch / brief dropout] Speaker 6: (inaudible)

[10:05] Aisha: on tool-calling, we need the model to ask clarifying questions, call internal claim APIs to pull up existing claim status, and then write back a note. everything must go through a proxy that redacts PII before leaving the VPC. is that supported?
[10:20] Diego: yes — we support function/tool calling and you can chain a pre-processing layer to redact or token-map PII. for Private deployments, the whole control plane can be in your VPC and calls never traverse public internet. for Hosted we provide encryption, but data does hit Redwood control plane unless you choose Private.

[12:00] Marcus: how do you handle KV cache and session pins? when the model calls internal APIs do you keep a KV cache of prior responses? we're worried about stale info and leaks.
[12:12] Chris: KV cache is per-session and can be invalidated on update. for private/dedicated you can host the cache in your network for extra control. we also support TTLs and explicit evict calls.

[14:40] Priya: curious about quantization — can you run 4-bit or int8 models on Dedicated for lower cost? how does latency change?
[14:48] Diego: yes, we have quantization profiles. 4-bit reduces memory and cost but may increase latency a bit depending on kernels and sequence length; our runtime chooses optimized kernels per model/seq length. we can run benchmarks across shapes.

[16:05] John: do you have auto fallback if the dedicated pool is saturated? we need graceful degradation — can't have 500ms spikes or errors during peak.
[16:14] Sara: Redwood supports smart routing — you can configure fallback to a cheaper compatible model or a different region. for enterprise SLAs we can provision burst capacity.

[18:00] Aisha: what's the typical on-ramp for Private on-prem? we have some air-gapped requirements for certain workflows.
[18:10] Chris: Private can be VPC-hosted control plane or full on-prem package. air-gapped installations are possible but require professional services; timeline usually 6-10 weeks depending on network and security reviews.

[20:10] [Diego shares screen, link dropped in chat: "redwood/model-comparison-brief.pdf"]
[20:20] Diego: here are rough perf numbers — open models we curate and verify on our catalog, we provide latency profiles for 2k/8k/32k. note numbers vary by quantization and batch.
[20:35] Priya: can you share that spreadsheet with comparative costs for 8k vs 32k?
[20:40] Diego: yes I'll send a workbook — it includes token costs, estimated GPU-hours for Dedicated, and example configs (batching, kv cache settings).

[22:50] John: routing policies — can we split by latency vs cost? e.g., low-latency region for paying customers and cheaper region for lower-priority tasks?
[22:58] Sara: yes you can set routing policies by route or by model tag. we've seen customers route by user tier, country, or cost centers.

[24:30] Priya: SSO? we want SAML-based single sign-on and RBAC for developer-level keys.
[24:38] Sara: supported — enterprise tier includes SSO, RBAC, and per-route access control. we can also integrate with Okta or Azure AD.

[26:05] Marcus: about logs and auditing — we need immutable audit trail per request and integration with Splunk/ELK.
[26:12] Chris: we export structured logs and trace events; for private installs you can push logs to your SIEM and retain them per your retention policy.

[28:00] John: what's the recommended starting model? something balanced for summarization and multilingual?
[28:10] Diego: for your use case I'd recommend a 32k-capable Mistral-like variant for long context, but run an eval comparing it to a Llama-derivative and a smaller 8k quantized variant as a fallback. also set up a canary route to test hallucination/precision on your prompt set.

[30:15] Aisha: for fine-tuning — we might want to tune on our policy and claims examples. what's the path? managed fine-tune or run local fine-tune?
[30:25] Diego: both options. we offer managed fine-tuning on Dedicated/Hosted with private data handling or you can run training in your environment and deploy a model artifact. tuning sample size you mentioned ~50k examples would be enough to push Spanish and domain specifics.

[32:40] [brief crosstalk — someone muted/unmuted] Speaker 6: sorry — I had to step away for a second.

[33:05] Priya: benchmarks — for the pilot we'll need Redwood to run a 48-hour latency/cost benchmark with our prompt set and 8k vs 32k scenarios. can you run that or do we run locally?
[33:18] Sara: we can run it on our Dedicated test cluster or provide scripts to run in your environment. Diego will prepare a plan.

[35:00] John: pricing — ballpark what does Dedicated vs Hosted look like for our expected scale?
[35:10] Sara: ballpark — Hosted usage-based pricing tends to be higher per token but zero infra ops; Dedicated has fixed monthly pool pricing with lower unit cost at scale. we'll send a tailored example with your QPS and expected tokens per request.

[36:22] Marcus: security: if we go Dedicated but not Private, can we still bring our KMS and have keys not in Redwood's control?
[36:30] Chris: yes for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys and bring-your-own-key in many cloud regions; for complete key isolation Private is best.

[38:05] Aisha: do you have real-world references in insurance?
[38:12] Sara: we have a couple anonymized case studies — I'll include those links in the follow-up.

[40:00] Diego: next steps recap — we will: 1) send SOC2/security deck and private deploy checklist, 2) propose benchmark plan for 8k/32k with costing, 3) schedule infra deep-dive (VPC + KMS + audit logs), 4) run a small multilingual evaluation on English/Spanish/French using your sample prompts.

[41:20] Priya: timeline — if we get the docs and benchmark by mid-June we can start a pilot in late June. that's our internal timeline.

[42:10] John: perfect. a couple quick clarifying Qs — about tool-calling auth, can function calls be signed with our service account keys?
[42:20] Chris: yes, calls can be proxied through your gateway; we support signed tokens and mutual TLS for backend tool endpoints.

[44:00] Sara: any blockers?
[44:05] Marcus: just the security review and KMS details — once those check out we're good to run the pilot.

[45:10] Sara: okay we'll get the materials over in the next 48 hours. Diego, Chris will own the tech deliverables. Priya, John — please send the sample prompts and some traffic shape.

[46:00] John: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[46:05] Sara: thank you — we'll follow up with the links. bye.

Action recap (verbatim):
- Sara Patel: send SOC2 + security FAQ + private deploy checklist (due 2026-06-15)
- Diego Morales: benchmark plan for 8k/32k with cost estimates + model comparison workbook (due 2026-06-18)
- Priya Rao: provide anonymized sample prompts, expected QPS and traffic shape (due 2026-06-14)
